title: Speculative Trait Implementations (The Pragmatic Limit)
pattern: Implementing complex math, comparison, or custom traits on a struct 'just in case' it might be needed someday, with zero active callers.
why_bad: Increases binary size, extends compilation times, and leaves unused dead code that must be maintained, documented, and tested.
detection: An implementation block (`impl Trait for Type`) whose methods have zero active call sites.
counterexample: Public library designs where standard traits (`PartialEq`, `Clone`, `Debug`) are expected on all public structs.
fix: Delete the unused trait implementation block.
source: Fowler, *Refactoring*, Chapter 3 ("Bad Smells - Speculative Generality"); Sandi Metz, *Practical Object-Oriented Design*, Chapter 9.
